About

Engineering precision, leadership proven.

I'm a Mechanical Engineering student at De La Salle University – Dasmariñas, with hands-on Design and Manufacturing internship experience in conveyor and material-handling systems at R. Dan & Co., Inc. My work spans reverse engineering 2D drawings into 3D SolidWorks models, correcting GD&T discrepancies, and applying Finite Element Analysis to validate structural designs.

My technical toolkit covers SolidWorks, AutoCAD, GD&T, and FEA, paired with direct floor exposure to CNC machining, laser cutting, and bending operations, plus QA/QC inspection and procurement. I hold Lean Six Sigma and ISO 9001:2015 QMS credentials, with a CSWA certification in progress.

Outside the shop floor, I lead as Director for Sports and Recreation at JPSME – Cavite Chapter, running logistics for tournaments and events serving 100+ student participants and a 7-person officer committee — the same coordination discipline I bring to engineering projects.

Long-term, I'm working toward design and manufacturing roles in aviation, aerospace, automotive, and broader manufacturing engineering — industries where precision documentation and hands-on fabrication knowledge matter as much as CAD skill.

Portfolio Highlights

Featured projects.

Two industrial deliverables from my R. Dan & Co. internship, documented with real fabrication-floor and CAD evidence, plus a set of self-directed CAD studies.

BC10 Conveyor
MYSAN Company · R. Dan & Co., Inc.
₱18,000,000 build

Contributed to the design of the BC10 Conveyor — a pallet chain conveyor system built for MYSAN Company. Work included CAD modeling of structural sub-assemblies and drive-end components, cross-checked against fabrication drawings before release to the shop floor.

Parts I contributed
Drive-end frame assembly
Side panel & bracket detail
Multimix Project
MYSAN Company · R. Dan & Co., Inc.
₱54,000,000 build

Contributed the Leg Assembly design across the 525MMH, 575MMH, and 775MMH height variants used throughout the Multimix line — modeled in SolidWorks and cross-checked against fabrication drawings, then followed through to the welded assemblies on the shop floor. Also contributed the side bracket assembly used to mount adjacent conveyor sections.
